key_insight: Laser breakdown inside micrometer water droplets generates a plasma-driven pressure load that drives liquid-shell expansion and breakup, while ambient pressure mainly changes the emitted shock wave rather than the droplet’s deformation.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and control laser–droplet interactions in spray diagnostics, laser ablation, and microfluidic atomization where coupled gas–liquid shock dynamics matter.
method: Nanosecond laser-induced breakdown in micrometer water droplets under finite-beam focusing (D0/Db ~ 2).
Simultaneous measurement of droplet deformation and emitted shock waves across a range of ambient pressures.
Comparison of low- and high-energy regimes to distinguish interfacial bubble collapse from liquid-shell atomization.
evidence_signal: Experimental observations show low-energy interfacial bubble collapse and high-energy supersonic shell expansion, with shock propagation strongly affected by gas density but droplet morphology remaining nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The conclusions are drawn for a specific finite-beam, micrometer-droplet regime, so direct transfer to other droplet sizes, pulse durations, or focusing conditions may not hold.
paper_title: Ambient-pressure effects on shock emission and liquid-shell expansion following optical breakdown inside water droplets
